problem: For integers r>=2, k>=1, a_1..a_k>=1, b>=1 let P(q) = [a_1]_q...[a_k]_q * [b]_{q^r}, where [n]_q = 1+q+...+q^{n-1} and [b]_{q^r} = 1+q^r+...+q^{r(b-1)}. P is (weakly) unimodal if its coefficients satisfy c_0<=...<=c_m>=...>=c_N for some m. U = {b : P unimodal}, F = sum floor(a_i/r), D = sum(a_i-1). Question: exactly which parameters make P unimodal? (Source: arXiv:2605.12822, Conjecture 5.4.)

claims.statement: Theorem 1/Cor 1 (sandwich window for B* from M = max tau), Theorem 2 (bounds on M via L_k), Theorem 3 (growth order of the excess as k->infinity for fixed residue proportions with positive middle mass), Lemma 6.

Theorem 1 (window criterion), Theorems 2/3 (explicit L0 = max(1, floor((S-k+3-r)/2)) for large-part regime, S=sum(a_i-1)), Theorem 4 (universal necessity U(a) ⊆ [1,F+1] ∪ (F+U_inf)), Theorem 5 (two-chain structure of U_inf), Theorem 6 (U_inf ⊆ [1,T6-F]).
r>=4, r divides no a_i, exactly three a_i with middle residue, nm = #{a_i = -1 mod r}: if r<=30 and nm<=37 then U = [1,B*] with B* = T6 - 2*[tau_s<=-2 and s>=2mu], s=(D+1) mod r.

claims.description: Exhaustive check of Conjecture S2 (U = [1,B*] or [1,B*] minus {B*-1}, B* ≡ 1+F mod 2, when r divides no a_i) over all multisets with r in [4,8], 1<=k<=6, a_i in [2,2r+2], r dividing no a_i; computing U for each by exact unimodality checks over b up to T6+2.
claims.statement: Conjecture S2 holds on all 100,488 such parameter sets; B_main - B_off = 1 in 100,402 and 3 in 86 (B_main = max U, B_off = max element of U with parity F).

claims.description: Domain: r>=4, k=len(a)>=3, all a_i equal to a, s = a mod r in [2, r-2]; n = floor(a/r). (1) If b <= kn+1, P is unimodal. (2) Otherwise let e = b-1-kn and K = k(s-1)+1-r(2+e). This does not depend on n. Let tau_t = Gamma_t - Gamma_{t-1} (indices mod r), where Gamma_t = number of k-tuples in {0,...,s-1}^k whose sum is congruent to t mod r. Equivalently, tau_t = (2/r) * sum_{j=1}^{r-1} sin(pi j/r) * (sin(pi j s/r)/sin(pi j/r))^k * sin(pi j (k(s-1)+1-2t)/r). If n>=1, let h_j = sum_{l>=0, lr<=j} C(j-lr+k-2, k-2) for j>=0, i.e. the coefficients of 1/((1-q)^(k-1)(1-q^r)). If n=0, let h_j be the power-series coefficients of [s]_q^k (1-q)/(1-q^r). In both cases h_j = 0 for j<0. Then P is unimodal iff tau_{m mod r} + h_{K-m} - h_m >= 0 for each of the r integers m with K/2 - r <= m < K/2. Only positions with tau_m < 0 can fail. Consequences: for n>=1, U = [1,kn+1] united with (kn+1+E_inf(r,s,k)), so U depends on n only through the shift F = kn. E_inf has the form {odd e <= E_odd} united with {even e <= E_even}, with E_odd < E_even. B* = kn+1+E_even, and U is either [1,B*] or [1,B*] minus {B*-1}.
claims.statement: All-equal middle-residue family rule (R2E5) as described.
claims.numbers: 0 errors on 4,824,541 (instance,b) pairs: r=4..8 all n, r=9..30 with n in {0,1}, k=3..60, b<=T6+2.

claims.description: Domain: r>=4, r divides no a_i, and exactly three a_i have residue a_i mod r in [2,r-2]; every other a_i then has residue 1 or r-1. Compute tau = (1-q) * prod_i [a_i mod r]_q reduced mod (q^r - 1). This is a length-r integer vector with tau_t = Gamma_t - Gamma_{t-1}, and it depends only on the residues. Let mu = the largest j in [1,r-1] with tau_j > 0, or 0 if there is none; this is the mu of Theorem C. Let D = sum(a_i - 1), T6 = 1 + floor((D+1-2mu)/r) and s = (D+1) mod r. FIRE holds when tau_s <= -2 and s >= 2mu. Then B* = T6 - 2 if FIRE holds, otherwise B* = T6. Prediction: P is unimodal iff b <= B*, so U = [1,B*] is always an interval. B* - 1 - F is even and >= 0. Over all residue data with r<=30, FIRE occurs only when s = r-2 and tau_{r-2} = -2. FIRE depends only on (r, the middle residues, and the count of residue r-1 elements mod 2r), so it does not depend on F or on the sizes of the a_i.
claims.statement: Three-middle-residue rule (R2E8): U=[1,B*], B* = T6 - 2*[tau_s<=-2 and s>=2mu].
